title: EgressPolicy
description: The full egress policy document: a set of named endpoint policies.

policies.description: Named endpoint policies. Evaluation iterates in document order; the first policy whose endpoint matches the destination is the one whose rules are consulted.

EgressEndpoint.description: One destination endpoint declared in the policy.

host.description: Hostname or IP (the preflight-checked value, never a raw user string — canonicalization is the caller's responsibility).

tls.description: TLS is required for this endpoint.

EgressEndpointPolicy.description: One named policy: an endpoint plus the ordered rules and the originating-component grant.

name.description: Human-readable policy name (the audit trail names this).

originating.description: Components permitted to use this grant. Empty means "all components".

EgressProtocol.description: The wire protocol of an egress endpoint.

oneOf.description: MCP (Model Context Protocol) over stdio or HTTP.

EgressRewrite.description: Per-endpoint rewrite flags: which placeholder-substitution points are active for this destination.

request_body_rewrite.description: Substitute placeholders in the request body.

EgressRule.description: One rule in an endpoint policy: a grant scoped to method, path pattern, and (for MCP) tool name.

methods.description: HTTP methods this rule matches (e.g. `["GET"]`). Empty means "all methods".

path_pattern.description: Path glob. `*` matches one segment; `/*` at the end matches any suffix. `/api/v2/tickets/*` admits `/api/v2/tickets/123` and refuses `/api/v2/tickets/123/comments`.

tool_names.description: For MCP rules: the tool names this grant covers. `None` means "all tools on this endpoint".

oneOf.description: Matching traffic is admitted; a denial is a hard refusal.
Matching traffic is admitted but an audit record is written identical in shape to a refusal — progressive rollout without schema change.
